_meta.description: Recorded vision results for the demo photos, used only by the vision stub when no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. Written by Claude (the coding agent) looking at each photo while building the prototype; not live inference from the app. With a key set, the app calls Claude live instead and these are ignored.

result.summary: Open roll-off container about three-quarters full of corrugated cardboard boxes, with some bubble wrap, plastic bags and taped packaging.

materials_seen.evidence: Opened and flattened corrugated boxes, packaging inserts, a few paper leaflets
Bubble wrap and clear plastic bags between the boxes

primary_stream.rationale: Almost all visible material is corrugated cardboard packaging.

contamination.rationale: Mostly clean, dry cardboard, but plastic film is visible in several places and may be close to the 5% limit for low.

volume_m3.basis: Only the top of a large open roll-off is visible; assuming a 25-30 m³ container about three-quarters full.

ewc_code.rationale: Boxes and transit packaging, so packaging waste (chapter 15) rather than municipal paper.

result.segregation_tip: Pull out the bubble wrap and plastic bags (about 6%) so the load stays a clean recycling grade.

result.summary: Overfilled builders' skip of mixed renovation waste: broken plasterboard and plaster, blocks and bricks, timber offcuts, insulation, plastic pipe and bin bags.

materials_seen.evidence: Broken plasterboard, plaster, concrete blocks and brick fragments
Timber battens and offcuts on top of the load
Yellow insulation, black bin bags, a dark storage unit
Plastic pipe, plastic sheeting and bags

primary_stream.rationale: Typical mixed renovation waste from a building site.

contamination.rationale: Inert rubble mixed with plasterboard, insulation and bagged general waste. The bags hide what is inside, so it could be high.

volume_m3.basis: Standard builders' skip (about 3.7 m long, 6 m³ level) heaped well above the rim; traffic cone for scale.

ewc_code.rationale: Mixed construction and demolition waste with no visible hazardous items.

hazard_flags: Old plaster, boards and insulation from a renovation: confirm the building's age and check for asbestos-containing materials before collection.
result.segregation_tip: Keep timber and plasterboard in separate skips: clean timber can go to wood recycling and plasterboard to gypsum recycling, which lowers the gate fee.

result.summary: Large pile of softwood pallets in a depot yard, many broken, with loose boards and a stretch-wrapped stack of pallet scrap.

materials_seen.evidence: Untreated softwood pallets and pallet boards

contamination.rationale: Clean wood, but many pallets are broken and some are wrapped in film, which matches medium rather than low.

volume_m3.basis: No container; estimated from euro pallets (1.2 × 0.8 m) stacked roughly 2 m high over several metres. Rough.

result.segregation_tip: Set aside the intact pallets: graded as low contamination they qualify for pallet reuse, which pays a rebate instead of a gate fee.

result.summary: Open roll-off container about two-thirds full of mixed scrap metal: tube frames, wire shelving, a rusty fire bowl and a small appliance, with plastic parts mixed in.

materials_seen.evidence: Steel tube frames, wire mesh shelving, rusty steel bowl
Plastic parts: a child's scooter, tool handles
Fabric, a small electrical appliance and some wood

contamination.rationale: Mixed metals with plastic and fabric attached or mixed in.

volume_m3.basis: Large open roll-off (about 6 m long) roughly two-thirds full; loose, airy load.

ewc_code.rationale: Mixed metals. 17 04 05 would apply if it were sorted iron and steel only.

hazard_flags: A small electrical appliance is visible: electrical equipment belongs in a separate WEEE stream.
result.segregation_tip: Remove the plastic parts and the appliance to sell the load at the clean-metal rebate.
